title: Post-incident: Noise containment playbook and reservation sizing adjustments for Dedicated clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
During the March 2026 peak, one Dedicated cluster experienced a multi-hour degradation due to a combination of a single tenant generating unusually high concurrent streaming requests (noisy neighbor), a set of reservations that were undersized relative to observed traffic patterns, and an overly permissive burst policy that allowed transient demand to starve steady-state workloads. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, proposed mitigations, and a phased rollout plan to reduce recurrence risk and improve customer SLOs.

Root causes identified:
1) Noisy tenant produced sustained concurrent sessions with long KV-cache lifetimes, causing eviction pressure and GPU memory churn.
2) Reservation sizing was based on historical average throughput; recent model changes increased per-request token processing and caused steady-state reservations to be insufficient.
3) Burst policy allowed unlimited short-term concurrency using cluster spare capacity; without a graceful backoff the burst consumption prevented reservation reclaim and delayed autoscaler response.

Impact observed:
- 3 production customers experienced elevated tail latency and token drop rates for 110 minutes.
- Increased evictions triggered fallback to smaller model variants for internal traffic routing for ~90 minutes.
- Pager awakenings and two customer incident escalations (one enterprise SLA breach narrowly avoided via manual routing).

2026-03-06 Priya (SRE): Deployed temporary quota cap for offending tenant to stabilize cluster. Metrics normalized within 18 minutes. Recommend automation to avoid manual intervention next time.

2026-03-10 Marco: Implemented simulation harness to replay tenant traffic and validate reservation-sizing heuristics. Found that 30% headroom above p95 throughput covers typical model-version rollout spikes.

2026-03-14 Marco: Action plan approved by infra leadership. Began work on soft-reserve implementation (see artifacts).
mitigation_plan:
Short-term (<=2 weeks):
- Add tenant-level soft quota enforcement (rate cap + session cap) configurable by SRE.
- Adjust burst policy to use a token-bucket with decay and per-tenant share; enforce a hard cap on sustained burst consumption per reservation.
- Update runbook with immediate steps to throttle noisy tenants and escalate to on-call SRE.

Medium-term (2-8 weeks):
- Implement reservation autosizing heuristic: compute reservation target = max(historical 95th, incoming forecasted 75th * 1.3). Use replay harness to validate across recent model versions.
- Introduce a predictive eviction buffer: reserve 8-12% GPU memory headroom to reduce KV-cache churn during transient spikes.
- Expose per-reservation burst-credits metric in Console and add alert when a reservation consumes >40% of cluster burst for >5 minutes.

Long-term (8-16 weeks):
- Enhance scheduler to support tenant-weighted isolation: ensure minimum steady allocation for reservations even while allowing limited burst across shared pool.
- Add QoS tiers that let customers opt into guaranteed headroom at higher price points.
- Bake learnings into autoscaler: consider burst-aware scale-up decisions so autoscaler differentiates between transient bursts and steady load growth.
acceptance_criteria: Automated replay shows no latency regression for steady tenants when a noisy tenant generates 3x historical peak for 30 minutes.
Soft-reserve prototype merged and feature-flagged with unit and e2e tests in runtime-1.22 branch.
New Console metrics and alerting present: per-reservation burst-credit usage and reservation headroom percentage.
Runbook appended with step-by-step tenant throttling and a post-escalation checklist; SRE on-call runbook drill completed.
Customer-facing incident summary drafted and reviewed with legal/PR for affected customers.
